steps.title: Styles and structure
steps.body: Instead of loose formatting, use the Styles (the 'Normal text' menu at the top): Heading 1, Heading 2, Title. Via Insert > Table of contents you automatically build a table of contents from your headings. That keeps a longer document organized.

steps.title: Working on one document together
steps.body: Click Share and enter email addresses. Choose 'Editor', 'Commenter' or 'Viewer'. Everyone sees changes live. With Comments (right-click on text) you give feedback, and via File > Version history you restore older versions.

steps.title: Templates, checking and PDF
steps.body: Pick a ready-made template for a letter, résumé or meeting notes via the Template gallery. The spell check is under Tools. Want to email it as an attachment? File > Download > PDF Document.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a document with a Heading 1, a table and a table of contents, share it with someone and ask for one comment.

steps.title: Using formulas
steps.body: A formula always starts with =. Examples: =SUM(B2:B10) adds up, =AVERAGE(B2:B10) gives the average and =B2*C2 multiplies. Refer to cells instead of typing numbers: if a number changes, Sheets recalculates by itself.

steps.title: Filtering and staying organized
steps.body: Choose Data > Create a filter to sort and filter (for example all expenses above €50). With View > Freeze your top row stays put while scrolling. Working with multiple tabs? Give them clear names.

steps.title: Making a chart
steps.body: Select your data and choose Insert > Chart. A bar chart is good for comparing (spending per month), a pie chart for splitting up. Sheets suggests a suitable type itself, and you adjust it on the right.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a household budget for three months, calculate totals and the average with formulas and add a chart.

lessons.title: Google Slides: a presentation that sticks

steps.title: One message per slide
steps.body: Put one point on each slide, with short text and preferably an image rather than a wall of text. No more than six lines per slide. Don't read your slides out word for word — add something to them.

steps.title: Theme and layout
steps.body: Choose a theme via Slide > Change theme and stick to it: the same colors and fonts. Use Slide > Apply layout for fixed formats. Add a chart from Sheets via Insert > Chart > From Sheets.

steps.title: Presenting and sharing
steps.body: Write your story in the speaker notes under your slide. With Present you show the slides; with Share colleagues can collaborate. During a video meeting you share your screen or present directly in Google Meet.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a five-slide presentation for a work meeting or neighborhood meeting, with a theme, one chart and notes on every slide.
